title: Run-Length Encoding
statement:
Run-Length Encoding (RLE) is a simple compression technique. Given a string S of lowercase English letters, encode it by replacing consecutive runs of the same character with the character followed by the count of consecutive occurrences.

Then, given a positive integer Q, answer Q queries. Each query gives an index K (1-indexed) into the decoded (original) string, and asks what character is at that position.

The original string can be extremely long (up to 10^14 characters), so you must NOT decode the full string. Instead, use the encoded form to answer each query efficiently.
constraints:
1 <= |S| <= 10^5
S contains only lowercase English letters.
Each run count fits in a 64-bit integer.
1 <= Q <= 10^5
1 <= K <= length of decoded string
inputFormat:
Line 1: the string S.
Line 2: Q (number of queries).
Lines 3 to Q+2: each line contains one integer K.
outputFormat: For each query, print the character at position K (1-indexed) of the decoded string.

examples.explanation: Decoded string: aabbbcccc. Position 1 = 'a', position 4 = 'b', position 9 = 'c'.

s = input().strip()
q = int(input())
queries = [int(input()) for _ in range(q)]
